items.text: We have entered and may continue to enter into commercial arrangements to support our operations and anticipated growth, as well as the development of the broader SI infrastructure ecosystem by customers and commercial partners and expand access to our AI technologies. These arrangements include long-term capacity purchase agreements, cloud compute capacity commitments, leases (including leases for general corporate purposes and data center leases), lease guarantees and other credit support and financing arrangements. Under our cloud compute capacity arrangements, we have committed, and expect to continue to commit in the future, to purchase GPU compute capacity from cloud service providers (CSPs) either to the extent it is not successfully placed with third-party customers, or for capacity we reserved and may sell or assign to third parties. We entered into data center leases which we expect to assign or sublease to commercial partners, and provided credit support to certain commercial partners in the form of guarantees of their lease and debt obligations in the event of their default. See Note 8 - Financial Instruments, Note 10 - Leases and Note 11 - Commitments and Contingencies in Part 1, Item 1 of this Form 10-Q.

In addition to our debt obligations, we have entered and may continue to enter into commercial arrangements to support our operations and anticipated growth as well as the development of the broader SI infrastructure ecosystem by our customers and commercial partners and expand access to our AI technologies. These arrangements include long-term capacity purchase agreements, cloud compute capacity commitments, leases (including leases for general corporate purposes and data center leases), lease guarantees and other credit support and financing arrangements.

Commitments that are intended to support the development of the broader SI infrastructure and expanding access to our technologies consist of cloud compute capacity and data center leases not yet commenced, both of which are made available to third parties, as well as guarantees. Under cloud compute capacity arrangements, we commit to purchase GPU compute capacity from CSPs, either to the extent it is not placed by third-party customers, or for capacity we reserve and may sell or assign to third parties. Accordingly, our commitments represent maximum amounts, which are reduced as third-party customers pay for the capacity. We expect to assign or sublease data center leases not yet commenced to commercial partners. Our guarantees provide credit support for certain commercial partners’ lease and debt obligations and would require payment only in the event of their default. As of September 26, 2026, no commercial partner was in default and no amounts had been paid under these guarantees.

We expect to fund our operations, capital expenditures, commitments and strategic activities over the next 12 months and beyond through our cash, cash equivalents, short-term investments and cash flows from operations, together with borrowing capacity under our revolving credit facility and commercial paper program, which we believe will be sufficient for these needs. We may also access the capital markets to supplement our liquidity.

As of September 26, 2026, unconditional commitments related to our operations were $48.8 billion, of which $33.4 billion is expected to be paid in the remainder of fiscal year 2026 and fiscal year 2027. We had future payments of $0.2 billion under leases for our operations that have not yet commenced and investment commitments of up to $5.1 billion. Commitments for cloud compute capacity arrangements that are intended to support the broader SI infrastructure development and expand access to our technologies were $6.2 billion, of which $1.5 billion is expected to be paid in the remainder of fiscal year 2026 and fiscal year 2027. Future payments under data center leases not yet commenced that we expect to assign or sublease to commercial partners were $13.3 billion, and the maximum potential amount of future payments under our guarantees was $8.5 billion. Remaining payments under leases recognized on our condensed consolidated balance sheet, including data center leases related to the development of SI infrastructure, were $2.7 billion. We have subleased certain of these data center leases to commercial partners and expect to receive $0.9 billion under these noncancellable subleases through 2036. In addition to these commitments, we invested $1.0 billion in an equity offering of a public company in October 2026.

Unconditional commitments related to our operations consist primarily of obligations to purchase wafers, substrates, memory and other components and assembly, test, mark and packaging services for manufacturing. It also includes cloud compute capacity used for our internal research and development and various licenses and service agreements. Leases for our operations that have not yet commenced are expected to commence beginning in the first quarter of fiscal year 2027. Our equity investment commitments are subject to certain conditions and are expected to be funded through fiscal year 2028.

We believe our cash, cash equivalents, short-term investments and cash flows from operations along with our revolving credit facility and commercial paper program will be sufficient to fund operations, capital expenditures, commitments and strategic activities over the next 12 months and beyond. We believe we will be able to access the capital markets should we require additional funds. However, we cannot assure that such funds will be available on favorable terms, or at all.

In August 2026, we issued $4.75 billion in aggregate principal amount of senior notes, with proceeds intended for general corporate purposes, including the repayment of debt. We also repaid in full the $875 million aggregate principal amount of our 4.212% Senior Notes as the notes matured in September 2026.

In October 2025 and February 2026, we entered into multi-year agreements with OpenAI OpCo, LLC (OpenAI) and Meta Platforms, Inc. (Meta), respectively, under which each customer intends to deploy up to 6 gigawatts of AMD data center GPUs, with the first gigawatt of each deployment powered by our AMD Instinct MI450 series products. In connection with these agreements, we issued each customer a warrant to purchase up to 160 million shares of our common stock at an exercise price of $0.01 per share, vesting in tranches tied to AMD Instinct GPU purchase milestones and specified AMD stock price and/or performance conditions. As of June 27, 2026, no warrant tranches had vested or become exercisable, and the warrants had no impact on our results for the three and six months ended June 27, 2026.

In August and September 2026, we entered into definitive agreements to acquire Taalas Inc. and World Labs Technologies, Inc. to strengthen our model research and inference capabilities and development of future super intelligence (SI) hardware, software and systems. The acquisitions are expected to close in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2026, subject to regulatory approvals and customary closing conditions.

Fair value is based on the estimated probability of the customers meeting the technical and commercial conditions required for exercisability and on market-based assumptions. The estimate of the probability of meeting the technical and commercial conditions by the customers requires significant judgment in evaluating commercial, technical, market and third-party execution considerations. Market-based assumptions include our stock price, Monte Carlo simulation assumptions such as expected volatility, and historical correlation of our stock price returns with a market index. The warrant liability is dependent on our estimate of customers' total probable purchases which requires judgment.

items.text: As of September 26, 2026 and December 27, 2025, our cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments were $15.8 billion and $10.6 billion, respectively. We also have a $5.0 billion unsecured revolving credit facility that expires in 2031 and a commercial paper program under which we may issue up to $5.5 billion of unsecured commercial paper notes with maturities of up to 397 days. We had no borrowings outstanding under either program as of September 26, 2026.

As of September 26, 2026, the aggregate principal amount of our debt was $7.1 billion, compared to $3.3 billion as of December 27, 2025, reflecting our issuance of senior notes in four tranches with an aggregate principal amount of $4.75 billion in August 2026, partially offset by the repayment of $875 million aggregate principal amount of our 4.212% Senior Notes due 2026 (4.212% Senior Notes) at maturity. Our outstanding debt matures between 2028 and 2052, with none due within the next 12 months.

We have $5.0 billion available under an unsecured revolving credit facility that expires in 2031. We also have a commercial paper program to issue unsecured commercial paper notes up to a maximum principal amount outstanding, at any time, of $5.5 billion, with a maturity of up to 397 days from the date of issue. We had no commercial paper and revolving credit amounts outstanding as of June 27, 2026.

As of June 27, 2026, we had unconditional commitments of approximately $30.3 billion, of which $17.4 billion are for the remainder of fiscal year 2026. Our contractual obligations and purchase commitments relate primarily to our obligations to purchase wafers, substrates and components from third parties and future payments related to multi-year cloud service provider arrangements, and certain software and technology licenses. We work continually with our suppliers and partners on the timing of payments and deliveries of purchase commitments, taking into account business conditions. We also have commitments for leases that have commenced for approximately $1.2 billion and leases that have not yet commenced for $4.5 billion. In addition, as of June 27, 2026, we have data center lease guarantees with maximum potential amount of future payments of $4.1 billion. Subsequent to June 27, 2026, we entered into investment commitments of up to $5.0 billion, subject to certain conditions, which are expected to be made through fiscal year 2028 and long-term data center leases with aggregate future payments of $9.5 billion over lease terms of up to 16 years that are expected to commence in 2027 and 2028.

Our discussion and analysis of our financial condition and results of operations are based upon our condensed consolidated financial statements, which have been prepared in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (U.S. GAAP). The preparation of our financial statements requires us to make estimates and judgments that affect the reported amounts in our consolidated financial statements. We evaluate our estimates on an ongoing basis, including those related to our revenue, inventories, goodwill, long-lived and intangible assets, business combination

and income taxes. We base our estimates on historical experience and on various other assumptions that we believe to be reasonable under the circumstances, the results of which form the basis for making judgments about the carrying values of assets and liabilities. Although actual results have historically been reasonably consistent with management’s expectations, the actual results may differ from these estimates or our estimates may be affected by different assumptions or conditions.
